page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.cm4.3xlarge is a general-purpose virtual machine instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture with 12 dedicated physical cores and 12 vCPUs, utilizing an Intel Xeon 8369HB processor running at 3.2 GHz. The instance is configured with 48.0 GB of system memory, providing a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per core. It does not include local storage or bundled GPUs, and it delivers a baseline network bandwidth of 4 Gbps.

Benchmark results place this instance consistently in the average performance tier for most workloads. It achieves a Geekbench single-core score of 1257.0 and a multi-core score of 6091.0, alongside a Passmark CPU score of 13441.38. Memory performance shows a read-only small block bandwidth of 698.22 GB/sec, though large block uncached read and write speeds drop to 55.6 GB/sec and 46.36 GB/sec respectively, resulting in a weak Passmark memory score of 1777.75. For specialized tasks, the CPU supports AVX-512 vector and deep learning instructions, enabling 755.34 tokens/sec for small 135M LLM prompt processing, though performance drops significantly to 17.38 tokens/sec on medium 7B models.

Given its dedicated CPU allocation and balanced resource density, the ecs.cm4.3xlarge offers stable, predictable performance for general-purpose workloads without the risk of resource contention. The lack of local storage means users must rely on network-attached storage, which is a key architectural tradeoff to consider. This instance is well-suited for applications such as static web serving, where it achieves a throughput of 7.8 GB/sec, Redis database operations, software compilation, and moderate text or image processing tasks.
